**voting**
cover.lead: The value that appears more than half the time, with one candidate and one count.
cover.use_it_when: You need the value that appears more than half the time, with O(1) extra space.
cover.why_it_matters: It finds a majority without a hash map: two variables, one pass.
cover.promise: You'll write Moore's voting in {lines} lines.

slides.title: Pair off and leave
slides.scene: At a party, people who want different drinks pair up and leave together. If one drink has over half the votes, its fans are the ones left.

blocks.text: Each pair takes away at most one tea. Tea has [[more than all the rest]], so tea is left.

slides.title: Count up or cancel
slides.lead: Count 0? This vote is the new candidate. Same as the candidate: +1. Different: −1.

quickcheck.question: Moore's voting on 5 4 4. Which candidate comes out?
quickcheck.answer: Answer: {{majority_element([5, 4, 4])}}. 5 and the first 4 cancel, so the last 4 is new.

blocks.text: There is no majority, but the loop still returns [[{{majority_element(NOMAJ)}}]].
If a majority isn't promised, count the candidate once more: keep it only if it appears over n/2 times.

slides.title: Majority element
slides.explain: Line 5 picks a new candidate when the count hits 0. Lines 7 to 10 vote for or against it.

slides.teaser: The bug that invents a majority
slides.title: Verify if not promised
slides.lead: The loop always returns someone, majority or not.

cost.note: A hash map also works, with O(n) space.

blog.summary: Find the value that appears more than half the time, with one candidate and one count.
blog.tested_inputs: hand-picked cases (one value, the LeetCode examples, values at ±1,000,000,000) and random arrays of up to 15 values with a majority mixed in, plus one array of 3,000 values
blog.tested_extra: The votes, the answer and the no-majority result come from running the code.

caption.first: Moore's voting for LeetCode 169 Majority Element: one candidate and one count find the over-half value in one pass.
lines: The trap: with no promised majority, 1 2 3 still returns 3. Verify it.
